_comment: Quality targets used by the mobile node to judge every flow. Each check has pass_at (the objective), hard_at (a limit past which the flow is Poor, null when the standard gives none) and a source. verified=true means the number was read from the ITU-T or IETF document itself. verified=false means it is our own project policy or could not be read from the document. A check that misses pass_at but stays inside hard_at makes the flow Fair. A check past hard_at makes it Poor.

standards.G.1010: ITU-T G.1010 (11/2001), End-user multimedia QoS categories, Appendix I, Tables I.1 and I.2
standards.Y.1541: ITU-T Y.1541 (12/2011), Network performance objectives for IP-based services, Table 1 (classes 0 to 5) and Table 3 (provisional classes 6 and 7)
standards.G.114: ITU-T G.114 (05/2003), One-way transmission time, clause 4
standards.G.107: ITU-T G.107 (06/2015), The E-model, clause 7 and Annex B
standards.G.113: ITU-T G.113 (09/2024), Transmission impairments due to speech processing, Appendix I
standards.RFC 3550: IETF RFC 3550, RTP, section 6.4.1 and appendix A.8

bpl.source: ITU-T G.113 Appendix I, G.711 with packet loss concealment (4.3 without)

codec_delay_ms.source: G.711 with 20 ms packets: one packet of sampling delay. Our simplification, not a table value

burst_r_min.source: Our simplification: BurstR is held at 1 or above so a total blackout cannot divide by zero

mouth_to_ear_delay_ms.label: One-way delay, mouth to ear
mouth_to_ear_delay_ms.source: ITU-T G.114 clause 4 (150 ms transparent, 400 ms planning limit) and G.1010 Table I.1 (under 150 ms preferred, under 400 ms limit)

network_delay_ms.label: Mean network delay
network_delay_ms.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 0, IPTD upper bound on the mean

jitter_ms.label: Jitter (RFC 3550)
jitter_ms.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 0, IPDV 50 ms. Y.1541 defines IPDV as a 1-10^-3 quantile minus the minimum delay. We compare RFC 3550 interarrival jitter to it, see PROTOCOL_NOTES

loss_pct.label: Packet loss, including late packets
loss_pct.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 0, IPLR 10^-3 (0.1 per cent) and G.1010 Table I.1, conversational voice, under 3 per cent PLR

mos.label: Listening quality, MOS (E-model)
mos.source: ITU-T G.107 Table B.1: R 80 (MOS 4.03) satisfied, R 60 (MOS 3.10) many users dissatisfied. Using 4.0 as the round number

g1010_delay_variation_ms.source: ITU-T G.1010 Table I.1, conversational voice, delay variation under 1 ms. Not used for the verdict: it describes the arrival variation before a playout buffer removes it, and Y.1541 gives the network figure we use instead. This reasoning is ours

playout_delay_ms.label: One-way delay incl. playout buffer
playout_delay_ms.source: ITU-T G.1010 Table I.1, videophone, under 150 ms preferred, under 400 ms limit (long-term targets)

network_delay_ms.label: Mean network delay
network_delay_ms.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 1, IPTD upper bound on the mean

jitter_ms.label: Jitter (RFC 3550)
jitter_ms.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 1, IPDV 50 ms (see the voice note on the definition)

loss_pct.label: Packet loss, including late packets
loss_pct.source: ITU-T Y.1541 Table 1, class 1, IPLR 10^-3 and G.1010 Table I.1, videophone, under 1 per cent PLR

freeze_ms.label: Frozen picture in the last window
freeze_ms.source: Project policy. No standard gives a freeze limit

text.title: Chat
text.g1010_category: Nearest row: e-mail server access (Table I.2). G.1010 has no instant messaging row

delivery_ms.label: Delivery time of a message
delivery_ms.source: ITU-T G.1010 Table I.2, e-mail server access, 2 s preferred and 4 s acceptable. Used as the nearest row, text chat is not listed

lost_messages.label: Messages lost
lost_messages.source: G.1010 Figure 2 places Messaging in the error intolerant row. The exact zero-loss cell for e-mail in Table I.2 was not read, so this is project policy
